mapping_authority: Belt associations: Nisarga direct instruction pt3378u; not a clinical diagnostic map.

modules.name: MER Self-Empowerment Training
modules.vocabulary: Self-empowerment, pro-active participation and the major hinges of the spine: lumbar / sacral, diaphragm, heart, thoracic inlet, atlas / occiput and pelvis.
modules.areas: Back, posterior neck, skull base and upper shoulders; connect with the pelvis and comfortable breath.
modules.question: Where are you working hard to hold yourself up?
modules.watch_for: Do not turn deep-pressure preference into a pressure target. No end-range neck movement or default deep anterior-neck work.
modules.mapping_note: The ocular association is Nisarga’s cross-reference through neck / skull-base support, not an instruction to perform eye work from MER1.
modules.official_title: MER Self-Empowerment Training: Back, Neck, Pelvis & Breath

modules.name: MER Grounding Training
modules.vocabulary: Grounding: contact through the feet, legs and hips; connect lower-body support with the whole person.
modules.areas: Plantar foot, calf, posterior thigh and quadriceps; hips as assessment indicates.
modules.question: Can the legs feel both supported and able to move?
modules.watch_for: Screen burning knee symptoms before deeper or loaded leg work. No direct pressure into a painful knee or forced stretch.
modules.mapping_note: Strong pelvic / legs level invites a check, not a conclusion that grounding is deficient.
modules.status: manual-sourced choices; lower-limb symptom screen required
modules.official_title: MER Grounding Training: Feet, Legs & Hips

modules.name: MER Centering Training
modules.vocabulary: Centering ability, pelvic balance, pelvis–heart connection and the felt sense of whole-body breathing.
modules.areas: Sacrum, gluteal attachments and sacral / gluteal fascia; connect the pelvis and spine.
modules.question: When stress rises, what support would make it easier not to brace?
modules.watch_for: Reported holding does not prove a pelvic tilt. Respect consent and boundaries; no automatic psoas or intimate pelvic-floor techniques.
modules.mapping_note: Work peripherally first; ask about felt holding rather than infer an emotional or sexual history.
modules.official_title: MER Centering Training: Pelvis & Core Integration

modules.name: MER Original Face Training
modules.focus: Face, Cranium, Neck, Arms & Vagus nerve
modules.vocabulary: Original Face: releasing and balancing the face, cranium, neck, breath and arms; natural movement in scalp, forehead and jaw.
modules.areas: Posterior neck and skull base; forehead, external jaw and scalp only where a relevant need is confirmed. The manual also includes upper-back / shoulder work.
modules.question: Can your head feel supported without having to hold it?
modules.watch_for: No orbital or intraoral work by default. Do not infer emotion from the face, gaze or build. No vagus stimulation / reset promise.
modules.mapping_note: The official training title includes Vagus nerve. The available manual does not provide a separate validated vagus-nerve technique for this report.
modules.status: manual-sourced choices; face / jaw / neck work conditional
modules.official_title: MER Original Face Training: Face, Cranium, Neck, Arms & Vagus nerve

modules.name: MER Inspiration Training
modules.focus: Opening the Breath, Thorax and Diaphragm
modules.vocabulary: Inspiration: opening the breath through thorax, shoulders and diaphragm; chest–rib–arm relationships with pro-active participation.
modules.areas: Pectoral region, lateral ribs, shoulder / arm relationship; diaphragm only after a relevant restriction is confirmed.
modules.question: Does your breath feel free, or is there an area you would like more space?
modules.watch_for: A saved diaphragm watch level does not override a report of free breath. No forced inhalation or automatic subcostal work.
modules.mapping_note: Diaphragm work MER5-013, PDF p.11, is not a default. Chest / shoulder integration can be considered without calling the breath restricted.
modules.status: manual-sourced choices; breath restriction requires confirmation
modules.official_title: MER Inspiration Training: Opening the Breath, Thorax and Diaphragm

modules.name: MER Fluid Body Training
modules.vocabulary: Fluid Body: joint release and joint mobilization, approached as a whole-body modality.

vocabulary_source.section: The MER modules & how to become a fully certified practitioner

modules.areas: Whole-body joint / movement context; abdominal region is Nisarga’s routing association, not a sourced abdominal technique.
modules.question: What do you notice in your belly as you breathe comfortably?
modules.watch_for: No Fluid Body manual is in the database. No specific joint maneuver, target muscle, timing or hands-on abdominal prescription is assigned.
modules.mapping_note: Modality-level signpost only; request the manual before adding technique-level content.
modules.status: modality-only; no manual or stroke database
modules.official_title: MER Fluid Body Training: Joint Release & Joint Mobilization

modules.name: MER Trauma Release Training
modules.vocabulary: Non-judgmental body reading, positive qualities, open curiosity, load and movement; posture as possibility, not a fixed story.
modules.areas: Felt experience across all selected regions. Muscles come from the linked MER1–5 strokes, not from emotional assumptions.
modules.question: Where does your body need support today?
modules.watch_for: Stay with permission and the client’s meaning. No trauma diagnosis, catharsis target or appearance-based emotional labels.
modules.mapping_note: A layer across every module and session, not a requirement to add a separate trauma session.
modules.status: cross-cutting questions and approach; no new stroke prescriptions
modules.official_title: MER Trauma Release Training: Breath, Fascia & Emotional Release
